summary: Argues nullable properties are safer than lateinit for deferred Android initialization: the compiler forces a null check (?, !!) at every use site, preventing the silent UninitializedPropertyAccessException that a missing isInitialized guard lets through. Contrasts both approaches with code.

Cloudy's blur-only Modifier.cloudy grows into Mirage, a general Compose Multiplatform shader system: write one common-source kernel that lowers to AGSL/SKSL, and compose ordered effect chains (duotone, iridescence, specular glint) via a sealed Optic API over a node's content or captured backdrop.

Explains Compose's three render phases (composition, layout, drawing) and shows how reading fast-changing state directly in a composable body forces full recomposition; switching to lambda-based Modifier.offset/graphicsLayer and passing lambdas instead of values defers the read to layout or draw for cheaper drag updates.

Part 5 of a RecyclerView deep dive covers writing custom LayoutManagers, the dual-pass pre/post-layout pipeline behind predictive item animations, and stable IDs for cheaper rebinding, then contrasts that virtualization model with Compose LazyColumn's slot-table-based recomposition skipping.

Introduces Ktor Client as a Kotlin-first, coroutine-based alternative to Retrofit for Android networking, highlighting its JetBrains-built multiplatform support, modular plugin architecture, and lightweight footprint for calling REST APIs.

Compose Multiplatform release v1.12.10-alpha01+dev4447 bumps org.jetbrains.compose and material3 artifacts alongside lifecycle 2.11.10-alpha01 and navigation3 1.2.0-alpha03 — an alpha dependency-version sync with no described API changes.

Promotional guide for downloading, registering, and logging into the PAK5D gambling/gaming APK in Pakistan, covering install steps and deposit bonus tiers. Not related to Kotlin, Android, or KMP development.

Overviews the new Android CLI, a terminal tool built for AI-agent workflows: project scaffolding, emulator and SDK management, APK deployment, doc search, UI hierarchy inspection, and direct Android Studio integration (find-usages, render-compose-preview) for scripted, non-IDE development.

Abdal PacketView captures Android network traffic locally via VpnService, attributing packets to the owning app by UID and exporting sessions as a pcapng file plus a JSON summary for deeper analysis in Wireshark or tshark.

An experimental Compose Styles API separates modifier chains that control appearance from those controlling behavior, addressing ordering bugs where paint and layout calls interacted unpredictably. Still experimental, it reshapes how Compose UI is organized without requiring an immediate rewrite.

A beginner-focused overview explains why Android developers should adopt Kotlin, contrasting it with Java through data classes, null safety, extension functions, smart casts, and coroutines, while noting full Java interoperability for gradual, file-by-file migration.
Arrow 2.3.0-alpha.2 resolves returnType more lazily in Arrow Optics, a small internal fix landed via a single pull request since the previous 2.3.0-alpha.1 pre-release.

Android Developers documents the TV Immersive list component, pairing a content row with a large preview pane that reveals background art and details as focus moves between cards, including anatomy, focus scaling, and 16:9 image guidance.

The Compose viewModel() API reference details overloads for creating or retrieving a ViewModel via CreationExtras, ViewModelStoreOwner, and factories, including a lambda-based initializer that gives direct access to createSavedStateHandle() for passing custom constructor arguments.

The androidx.lifecycle.viewmodel.compose package reference lists rememberViewModelStoreOwner, LocalViewModelStoreOwner, and the SavedStateHandle.saveable delegate family that bridges SavedStateHandle with Compose's rememberSaveable Saver API for persisting custom state holders like lists and maps.

A Wikipedia explainer on the XY problem describes how asking about an attempted solution instead of the underlying goal derails technical support conversations, illustrating why probing for root intent matters when troubleshooting developer questions.

JetBrains' Kotlin Language Server brings official LSP support to any editor, including a VS Code extension with IntelliJ-powered completion, diagnostics, and quick fixes. It supports Gradle/Maven builds and experimental Android Gradle Plugin projects; Kotlin Multiplatform support is still in development, and the server remains in Alpha.

KTConf 2026 announces two full-day, paid pre-conference workshops in Leuven: a "Kotlin Coroutines Forensics Masterclass" by Amanda Hinchman-Dominguez and "Kotlin Fundamentals" by Simon Vergauwen, each including lunch and coffee.

EnumStore is an experimental, now-unmaintained library that lets Kotlin enum entries double as Android DataStore preference keys, giving type-safe get/set calls and Flow/StateFlow-based reactive access without manually passing Context or raw string keys.

Kilua's animation module reimplements Compose's animate*AsState APIs (Double, Float, Int, Long, CssSize) for JS/Wasm targets on top of an external Motion-based spring engine, matching Compose Animation's default spring-physics behavior.

Jake Wharton's essay argues Jetpack Compose conflates two distinct things under one name: a general-purpose compiler/runtime that manages trees of nodes of any type, and Compose UI, the Android/Desktop rendering toolkit built on top of it. He contends sharing a name pigeonholes the runtime's broader potential beyond UI rendering.

Android Developers' ViewModel overview covers how ViewModel persists UI state and business logic across configuration changes, scoping via ViewModelStoreOwner, SavedStateHandle for process-death survival, and new Compose retain APIs like rememberViewModelStoreOwner/rememberViewModelStoreProvider for scoping ViewModels to individual lazy-list or pager items.

Android Developers documents ViewModel scoping APIs: viewModel() for the closest ViewModelStoreOwner, an explicit owner parameter for custom scopes, rememberViewModelStoreOwner()/rememberViewModelStoreProvider() for per-composable or per-page scoping (e.g. HorizontalPager items), and retrieving Navigation-graph-scoped ViewModels via getBackStackEntry().

Kraken Technologies cut average Gradle build time from ~6 minutes to ~1:50 and sync time from ~5 minutes to ~45 seconds across a 600-module KMP project by adopting the Dependency Analysis Gradle Plugin (DAGP) v3.16.1, which now finds unused/misclassified dependencies on JVM and Android targets (iOS analysis not yet supported).

Kotlin's official Multiplatform compatibility guide tracks supported Gradle/AGP/Xcode version ranges per Kotlin release and lists deprecation cycles: the androidTarget-to-android plugin migration, removed bitcode embedding, and default JVM Java source sets replacing withJava(). Answers a Slack question confirming AGP 9.2+ isn't yet officially supported.

GitHub source tree for kotlinx.coroutines' debug/internal package (DebugProbes, AgentPremain, ConcurrentWeakMap), linked in a Slack thread noting that most debug-agent logic actually lives in kotlinx-coroutines-core, so depending on these internals carries a low risk of incompatible changes despite being unsupported API.

Kotlin Foundation's 2026 grant program funds open-source Multiplatform libraries, tools, and frameworks, weighting selection toward security responsiveness and adherence to library best practices. First-round applications closed July 15, relevant to KMP maintainers seeking funding.

Kotlin 2.4.10 changelog covers fixes for K/Wasm multimodule incremental builds, K2 const-val annotation resolution, reified type inference with elvis inside lambdas, a Compose Compiler 2.4 stability-inference regression, Gradle BCV version-range resolution, JS Yarn lock handling, and scripting compiler-options annotations.

Maven Central listing for abi-tools-embeddable 2.4.0, JetBrains' standalone library for producing binary-compatibility-validator ABI dumps independently of Gradle, referenced in a Slack answer explaining that BCV in the Kotlin Gradle plugin only works against the current project.

Source for AbiValidationToolchain.kt, a new Kotlin Build Tools API (since 2.4.0) exposing programmatic ABI-dump and comparison operations for JVM classes/jars and klibs, letting tooling authors build binary-compatibility checks outside the Gradle plugin.
code_snippet:
val toolchain = kotlinToolchains.abiValidation
toolchain.dumpJvmAbiToStringOperationBuilder(
    appendable = System.out,
    inputFiles = listOf(jarFile)
).build()

summary: Kotlin 2.1.20 release notes: K2 kapt becomes the default plugin implementation, Lombok gains @SuperBuilder support, a new experimental executable {} DSL replaces Gradle's Application plugin for KMP JVM targets, Xcode 16.3 support lands, and the Compose compiler relaxes @Composable restrictions.

Experimental JetBrains ecosystem plugin for Declarative Gradle, letting Kotlin build scripts define jvmApplication, webApplication, and multiplatform library subprojects using the new .gradle.dcl declarative format instead of Kotlin DSL scripts, previewed at KotlinConf'26.

A community Ktor benchmark suite measures HTTP client throughput across CIO, Apache, OkHttp, and Java engines by firing concurrent request batches at a local Netty server. Useful for spotting client-engine regressions or gauging how configuration changes affect requests-per-second.

A dockerized follow-up benchmark isolates Ktor's HTTP client engines from their native counterparts (Apache, OkHttp, JDK) using CPU-pinned containers, finding a consistent 3.2-4.7x throughput gap. Profiling traces most overhead to kotlinx.coroutines scheduler internals, which consume over half the CPU time versus the wrapped library's own work.

Marketing page for Caddy, a general-purpose web server with automatic HTTPS/TLS certificate management, mentioned in a Ktor Slack thread as a reverse-proxy alternative to configuring TLS per client engine. Not itself Kotlin, Android, or KMP related.

Kotlin Compiler 2.3.20 introduced a regression where the frontend spawns coroutine Default Dispatcher threads without stopping them, leaking isolated classloaders and causing OOMs in large KSP-heavy builds. KSP 2.3.10 fixes this by moving its task cache to a Gradle build service.

KSP 2.3.9 paired with Kotlin 2.4.0 fails code generation for internal members, such as Hilt/Dagger @Provides functions, because Kotlin 2.4.0's new standardized module-name format injects a colon into generated identifiers that KSP/KotlinPoet cannot escape. Manually overriding moduleName works around it.

KSP2's KspAATask lost the NO-SOURCE task-skip optimization inherited from KSP1's KspTaskJvm because it declares source inputs as unfiltered file trees instead of restricting to *.kt/*.kts/*.java. Gradle can no longer detect source-less modules, forcing needless KSP reruns costing 300-500ms per module on full rebuilds.

KSP2's incremental build cache can silently drop generated output files for unmodified source files after an incremental run, so Gradle's post-build cache snapshot omits them and downstream compilation fails with unresolved references once restored. Reported as an open bug in KSP2's incremental processing.

KSP's KspAATask hashes source files without @NormalizeLineEndings, so a Windows checkout with CRLF line endings produces a different cache key than a Linux/macOS build with LF, causing every KSP task to miss the remote build cache cross-platform.

KSP's incremental compiler fails to record the dependency edge from an annotation argument (e.g. MyClass::class) through to the referenced class, so edits to that class don't mark dependents dirty and get skipped on rebuild.
code_snippet:
@MyAnno(MyClass::class)
class Annotated

summary: A merged KSP change switches AGP source consumption from sources.kotlin.static to sources.kotlin.all, letting KSP process Kotlin sources generated by other Gradle plugins or tasks instead of only its own outputs, without creating circular build dependencies.

A KSP fix addresses configuration cache invalidation for Kotlin/Native cross-compilation: onlyIf evaluated exported metadata JSONs at cache-store time before they existed, breaking reuse. It now declares them as task inputs and parses them at execution time.

A KSP PR memoizes KSTypeImpl.hashCode() behind a lazy-cached field instead of reopening an Analysis API session on every call, since it fires as a HashMap key hundreds of thousands of times per task; benchmarks showed roughly 400ms to 130ms.
code_snippet: private val cachedHashCode: Int by lazy { type.fullyExpand().hashCode() }

summary: A merged KSP fix corrects getJvmName for @JvmRecord data classes: Java records expose bare accessor names like name() rather than getName(), so ResolverAAImpl now checks for @JvmRecord alongside the existing bean-getter logic to avoid the wrong prefix.

A closed KSP task weighed bundling kotlinx.coroutines into KSP's uber jar, noting kotlin-stdlib doesn't reach it via reflection and that coroutines can be treated as an ordinary user-space dependency rather than a runtime library that needs shading in.

A closed KSP feature request proposed emitting a .dot graph from a given origin symbol showing every symbol reachable from it, to make missing edges in the incremental compilation dependency graph easier to spot while debugging.

Merged pull request in google/ksp flipping the default of the ksp.allow.all.target.configuration Gradle property to false, restricting which target configurations receive KSP processors automatically. Lands alongside KSP 2.3.10 fixes for coroutine-dispatcher OOMs and Kotlin 2.4.0 module-name sanitization.

Kotlin docs page on configuring KSP in multiplatform projects now that the catch-all ksp(...) configuration is deprecated. Shows adding processors per target (kspJvm, kspIosX64), stacking multiple processors on one target, and wiring test compilations like kspJvmTest.

JetBrains PyCharm blog roundup of agentic AI frameworks (LangChain, AutoGen, and others) comparing graph-based, role-based, and chain-based orchestration models for Python applications in 2026. A Slack commenter flags that JetBrains' own Koog framework is missing from the list.

First entry in a series on SoPhi, a Kotlin agent harness embedded in Spring Boot, explaining why the team wrote their own ~600-800 line agent loop instead of adopting Koog, LangChain4j, or Spring AI. Cites SoPhi's custom session format, TUI, and lazy skill loading as reasons no framework fit.

Content-farm style guide promoting the 'Raja Luck' gambling platform's Android compatibility and interface, padded with generic tips like keeping account details private and updating the device. Not Kotlin or Android development content.

Promotional guide for the 'BDG Game' gambling app describing its Android-friendly interface and generic usage tips such as securing accounts and using a stable connection. Not related to Kotlin or Android engineering.
Dev-channel release tag v1.12.0-beta03+dev4497 of JetBrains Compose Multiplatform, published July 20, 2026, with no changelog beyond the Maven coordinate bump for org.jetbrains.compose artifacts.

Android Developers Blog post announcing the Nearby Connections API will stop automatically turning on Wi-Fi and Bluetooth radios for first- and third-party apps, effective late 2026. Developers must manage radio state manually and prompt users to enable it themselves.

Explains rememberDecoratedNavEntries, a lower-level Navigation 3 API that pairs each independent NavBackStack with its own decorated NavEntry collection so rememberSaveable UI state survives tab switches, configuration changes, and process death without screen-level changes.

Assesses whether Jetpack Compose is production-ready for Android TV in 2026, covering D-pad focus handling, focus restoration, performance on fragmented TV hardware, Media3 playback integration, and migration paths from Leanback. Recommends Compose for new TV apps and gradual migration for existing Leanback codebases.

Weekly JVM/Kotlin roundup marking Kotlin's 15th anniversary and its multiplatform growth, plus a case study on how default JPA settings caused subtle performance and correctness bugs in a Kotlin microservice, alongside Spring Boot 3.x end-of-life notices.

Beginner walkthrough of Kotlin string handling: declaring strings, string templates and expression interpolation, concatenation, common String methods (trim, split, replace, case conversion), multiline strings, and structural equality, with Android-flavored examples like building API URLs.
code_snippet:
val price = 499
val quantity = 3
println("Total Price: ${price * quantity}")

summary: Promotional announcement for a paid book on data structures and algorithms for mobile developers across Android, iOS, Flutter, and Kotlin Multiplatform, covering complexity analysis and mobile-specific applications like caching and pagination; mostly a sales pitch with purchase links.
Personal Indonesian-language essay reflecting on religious judgment and mistreatment of marginalized people; unrelated to Kotlin, Android, or software development.

Release notes for Compose Multiplatform 1.12.10-alpha01+dev4500, bumping the core Compose and Material3 artifacts alongside Lifecycle 2.11.10-alpha01 and Navigation3 1.2.0-alpha03 dependency coordinates.
Release notes for Compose Multiplatform 1.12.0-beta03+dev4506, updating the core org.jetbrains.compose.* artifact coordinates to the new beta version with no further changelog detail provided.

Third post in Google's Jetpacker series covers cloud and hybrid AI on Android via Firebase AI Logic: URL/Search/Maps grounding for up-to-date chatbot answers, plus a hybrid-inference API with PREFER_ON_DEVICE, PREFER_IN_CLOUD, ONLY_ON_DEVICE and ONLY_IN_CLOUD routing modes to balance cost, latency and offline support.

Explains Android AppFunctions, which compile annotated Kotlin functions into type-safe tools a privileged on-device agent can discover via 'Android MCP', letting the Jetpacker demo app expose expense-tracking, itinerary and voice-note actions to voice/text commands without manual UI navigation.
code_snippet:
implementation("androidx.appfunctions:appfunctions:1.0.0-alpha10")
ksp("androidx.appfunctions:appfunctions-compiler:1.0.0-alpha10")

@AppFunctionSerializable(isDescribedByKDoc = true)
data class TripSerializable(
    val id: String,
    val title: String,
    val location: String
)

summary: Introduces Jetpacker, Google's open-source I/O demo travel app, and frames the 'Build intelligent Android apps' series: choosing on-device, cloud or hybrid inference for itinerary summaries, receipt OCR, chat translation and AppFunctions system integration depending on privacy, cost and capability needs.

Shows how to use Gemini Nano 4 via ML Kit's Prompt API and Structured Output API for on-device Android features in Jetpacker: summarizing trip itineraries and extracting structured data from receipt photos, with prompt tuning cutting response latency from 13 seconds to under 2.

JetBrains Air now connects to any ACP-compatible coding agent (GitHub Copilot, OpenCode, Cline, local Ollama models) alongside its bundled agents, adds IntelliJ-powered Java/Kotlin navigation and error diagnostics, Windows Docker task support, and an 'xhigh' reasoning effort option for Claude models.

RubyMine 2026.2 adds agentic debugging through a bundled debugger skill, native GitHub Copilot chat integration, third-party AI completion providers, and a symbol-based code insight engine enabled by default, plus RSpec 4 and RBS tooling improvements — a Ruby/Rails-only IDE release with no Kotlin/Android relevance.

PyCharm 2026.2 adds a Rust plugin for Python extension development, makes debugpy the default debugger, integrates the Pyrefly type engine, ships an editor minimap, AI-generated starter projects, and an agent skills manager — a Python-only IDE release with no Kotlin/Android relevance.

JetBrains Context is a new repository-intelligence layer that semantically indexes codebases so agents like Claude Code, Codex CLI and Junie can query relevant code instead of repeatedly re-exploring files; benchmarks show up to 68% fewer agent turns, 59% lower latency and 48% lower cost, across JetBrains IDEs, Air and VS Code.

JetBrains' Q2 2026 plugin developer newsletter covers Marketplace changes (internal API usage notices, an open Exceptions tab), an IntelliJ Platform Gradle Plugin 2.18.1 update, Plugin Verifier 1.409, and links to guides on remote development, UI responsiveness, and the newly open-sourced LSP client API.

A Medium review of a Udemy Jetpack Compose crash course finds it a solid refresher on animations, providers, and Compose fundamentals, but dated since it teaches Navigation 2 rather than the simpler Navigation 3.

A developer built a minimal IntelliJ timer/stopwatch plugin with Compose, Jewel, and Skiko, hosting composables via JewelComposePanel, keeping state in a project-level service as a sealed StateFlow hierarchy, and covering pitfalls around bundling Compose as platform modules across IDE major versions.

A nightly Compose Multiplatform alpha snapshot (1.12.10-alpha01+dev4525) bumps Material3, Lifecycle, and Navigation3 artifacts in lockstep; the release lists no specific changelog entries for this dev build.
Another Compose Multiplatform nightly (1.12.10-alpha01+dev4519) republishes the same Material3, Lifecycle, and Navigation3 dev artifacts a few hours before dev4525, again with no listed changes.
Compose Multiplatform ships a 1.12.0-beta03 dev build (dev4514) that bumps the core org.jetbrains.compose artifacts, with no specific changes documented in the release notes.

Arrow 2.3.0-alpha.4 updates the Optics compiler plugin to support generic types in the optics DSL and fixes it to work correctly alongside classes annotated with kotlinx.serialization's @Serializable.

Google guides Android developers on adapting apps for Samsung's new ultra-wide foldables and Wear OS 7, covering fluid layouts with Compose's new Grid/FlexBox/MediaQuery APIs, Window Size Classes, fold-aware design, CameraX for rotation-safe previews, and Wear Widgets via Jetpack Glance.

JetBrains Rider 2026.2 wires the IDE's coverage, profiler, and refactoring context into AI coding agents through bundled and installable skills, adds native GitHub Copilot integration, and ships WPF Hot Reload plus faster debugging and indexing for .NET and Unreal Engine projects.

RustRover 2026.2 adds axum/reqwest route-handler navigation, Ferrocene toolchain support, an interactive declarative macro tester, Criterion benchmark run configurations, and an agent skills manager for sharing framework knowledge across AI coding sessions.

First part of a series tracing how Android Views, Flutter, and Jetpack Compose each handle one state change: Views mutate a live tree via findViewById, Flutter rebuilds and diffs three parallel trees, framing why each rendering design trades efficiency differently.

Reflects on a senior-interview question -- why does Compose exist -- and walks through how View-based UIs scatter UI truth across separate widgets requiring manual synchronization, while Compose centralizes state in one UI-state object the framework keeps consistent.
code_snippet:
usernameText.text = user.name
progressBar.isVisible = false
followButton.isEnabled = false
toolbar.title = user.name
verifiedBadge.isVisible = user.isVerified
followersCount.text = user.followers.toString()

summary: Engineering guide to offline-first Android apps: Room as the single source of truth, an outbox table for durable pending writes, full/incremental/hybrid sync strategies, sync-token approaches, and field-level conflict resolution such as last-write-wins versus merge rules.
code_snippet:
@Entity(tableName = "outbox")
data class OutboxEntry(
    @PrimaryKey val id: String = UUID.randomUUID().toString(),
    val entityType: String,
    val entityId: String,
    val operation: Operation,
    val payload: String,
    val createdAt: Long = System.currentTimeMillis(),
    val retryCount: Int = 0,
    val lastError: String? = null
)

summary: Beginner-level walkthrough of Kotlin classes and objects covering properties, primary constructors, default values, init blocks, nested classes, and member functions, illustrated with Student/Product/User examples relevant to everyday Android model classes.
Weekly Jetpack artifact roundup: Media3 reaches 1.11.0-rc01 after a single beta, covering ExoPlayer, Transformer, session, Compose UI, and Cast modules, alongside new Gradle version-catalog releases.

CommonsWare retires cw-json in favor of kPointer, a Kotlin library that extracts values via JSON Pointer and dot-path syntax from JSON, YAML (yamlkt), and HTML/XML (Ksoup) through a shared adapter abstraction, with a conformance suite for custom adapters and future ports.

RustRover 2026.2 adds initial support for the Axum web framework, letting developers jump between route strings and their handler functions, see inline HTTP method/path hints, and auto-generate Reqwest client calls for an endpoint.

Rebuilds a voice-to-transaction Android feature entirely on-device, replacing the earlier Firebase AI Logic/Gemini cloud approach: whisper.cpp transcribes via JNI on a dedicated single-thread coroutine dispatcher, and a deterministic Kotlin parser (not an LLM) extracts the structured intent. Covers the Gradle/CMake NDK setup and the Hilt-swapped service interface.

Walks through exposing a Kotlin NoteRepository's CRUD methods as Android AppFunctions so an AI agent can discover and call them, documenting five gaps encountered between the alpha API's documentation and a working end-to-end integration.

Explains Kotlin's primary and secondary constructors, init blocks, constructor delegation, and default parameter values, with require()/check() validation examples and simple Android-style model classes like User and Product.

Describes how Play Store apps from publishers like mr.Bunn and Hadiz Studio request broad permissions to quietly turn devices into ad-traffic generators, framing policy-compliant but deceptive apps as a bigger everyday risk than classic malware.

Promotes BrowsePad, an app that turns a phone into a wireless touchpad and keyboard for browsing the web on Android TV via QR-code pairing over local Wi-Fi, covering gestures, desktop-site switching, tabs, and downloads.

Marketing listicle listing seven ways BrowsePad's phone-as-touchpad controller improves Android TV web browsing: cursor gestures, desktop-site rendering, multi-tab browsing, phone-based text input, bookmarks/history, and file downloads.

Overviews Android XR for developers: Home Space vs Full Space app modes, declarative spatial UI via Jetpack Compose for XR (panels, depth, 3D entities), the Compose Glimmer toolkit for smart-glasses micro-UIs, Gemini Live API voice integration, and the built-in Android Studio XR emulator.

GitHub release notes for Compose Multiplatform v1.12.10-alpha01+dev4541, a nightly dev build bumping the org.jetbrains.compose, material3, lifecycle, and navigation3 artifact coordinates in lockstep. No changelog text is provided beyond the version bump itself.

GitHub release notes for Compose Multiplatform v1.12.10-alpha01+dev4534, a nightly dev build one day earlier than dev4541, again bumping compose, material3, lifecycle, and navigation3 artifact versions together. No further details are included.

Shows how registering every destination directly inside Navigation 3's entryProvider turns it into an unmaintainable switchboard as an app grows. Proposes grouping related screens into EntryProviderScope extension functions per feature, so the root NavDisplay just composes feature entry points.

Argues Jetpack Compose screens need more than Loading/Success/Error booleans, covering cached content shown during refresh, filters retained across process recreation, and retryable errors that don't hide existing data. Recommends separating business-driven screen state from transient UI element state.

Walks through Kotlin property fundamentals: default getters/setters, custom getters for computed values, custom setters using the field backing keyword for validation, private setters, and lateinit. Includes Android-flavored examples like trimming email input and rejecting negative prices.

Walks through implementing FIDO2/WebAuthn passkey registration and login on Android with the Credential Manager API (androidx.credentials 1.5.0), wired into an MVVM ViewModel with sealed UI states and a minimal Compose screen that triggers the sign-in flow.

Covers building a production biometric login flow with BiometricPrompt and BiometricManager wrapped in MVVM, using a sealed AuthState and a Compose UI. Stresses signing a backend challenge with a Keystore-held CryptoObject rather than trusting a boolean success callback.

A consumer buying guide listing seven mistakes people make when purchasing a smartphone, covering brand bias, processor specs, camera megapixels, storage sizing, software update support, battery life, and trusting reviews. Not developer-focused content.
Promotional guide for a cross-platform teleprompter app covering script prep, four scrolling modes, and recording/editing across iPhone, Android, and web. Not Kotlin/Android development content.

JetBrains Compose Multiplatform alpha release bumping org.jetbrains.compose.* and material3 artifacts to 1.12.10-alpha01, plus lifecycle to 2.11.10-alpha01 and navigation3 to 1.2.0-alpha03, all under dev4546. A routine dependency-coordinate update for teams tracking the bleeding edge.

KSP 2.3.10 ships bug fixes including a fix for OOMs from unstopped coroutine dispatcher threads, by moving the KSP task cache to a Gradle build service. Recommended for projects hitting memory pressure during symbol processing.
